newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Sevel denies wrongdoing in 1992 IPO.
newsitem.headline: Sevel denies wrongdoing in 1992 IPO.

text.p: Car maker Sevel Argentina SA on Friday denied wrongdoing in its 1992 initial public offering and criticized a National Securities Commission investigation of the share flotation.

Sevel said in a statement that it wanted to make "a most emphatic declaration that the company and shareholders acted at all moments within the norms of current legislation and the rules established by the issue prospectus."
Sevel noted that the flotation came five years ago and said it had operated normally ever since, its shares had been listed continuously, and it had attracted numerous investors.
The National Securities Commission announced Thursday that it was launching a formal investigation into the June 1992 IPO, probing the company itself and a group of its then-directors.

The commission said its investigations had led it to suspect that "in the initial public offering of Sevel Argentina SA there was manipulation of the cut-off price via the introduction in the tender process of an offer financed by the sellers themselves."
The company said, "Sevel Argentina SA declares its unshakeable intention and vocation to defend the expectations of the public and, fundamentally, the legitimate interests of its shareholders."
Sevel makes cars under license from France's Peugot, which has a stake in the company.
